title: Adjacent / Adj
scramble: R U F2 R' U' R
notes: Two adjacent pieces need swapping (similar to T-Perm on 3x3)
story:
<!-- Case: Ortega-PBL-1 -->

## Overview
Adjacent swap on one layer: keep one face solved while you swap two adjacent pieces on the opposite layer.

## Recognition
- Hold the solved layer on the right; the front layer needs an adjacent swap.
- Opposite layer is already complete, so only one layer requires work.
- From above you see a three-cycle arrow on the unsolved layer.

## Technique
1. Execute `R U' R F2 R' U R'`.
2. Regrip back to neutral for any final AUF.

## Fingertricks
- Push `F2` with both thumbs simultaneously to keep the cube anchored.

## Common Mistakes
- Forgetting which face stays solved and accidentally disturbing both layers.

## Practice
- Alternate this case with Opp/Opp PBL to reinforce adjacent vs. opposite recognition.

## Related Cases
- [Ortega-PBL-2](deddal://case/Ortega-PBL-2)
- [Ortega-PBL-3](deddal://case/Ortega-PBL-3)

## Pro Tips
- Use the solved layer to gauge AUF before you start—the final alignment becomes trivial.
description: Two adjacent corners of same layer need to swap positions

title: Opposite / Opp
scramble: F2 U' R' U R U F2 U R U' R'
notes: Two opposite pieces need swapping (similar to Y-Perm on 3x3)
story:
<!-- Case: Ortega-PBL-2 -->

## Overview
Opposite/opp PBL: both layers show opposite pieces that must swap across the face, effectively two U-perms stacked.

## Recognition
- Neither layer is solved; each shows opposite colors facing each other.
- No adjacent matches anywhere on the cube.

## Technique
1. Run `R U' R' U' F2 U' R U R' U F2`.
2. Check both layers for AUF and finish.

## Fingertricks
- Count the rhythm “R U' R' U' – F2 – U'...” to keep from losing track mid-sequence.

## Common Mistakes
- Mixing it up with the diagonal case and running the wrong alg.

## Practice
- Drill opposite and diagonal swaps consecutively so you can spot the difference instantly.

## Related Cases
- [Ortega-PBL-1](deddal://case/Ortega-PBL-1)
- [Ortega-PBL-3](deddal://case/Ortega-PBL-3)

## Pro Tips
- Think of it as “two adj-swaps in a row”; this mental model helps you stay calm under pressure.

title: Diagonal / Opp Opp
notes: Easiest PBL case - only 3 moves, self-inverse
story:
<!-- Case: Ortega-PBL-3 -->

## Overview
Diagonal/opp-opp: both layers need diagonal swaps—the quickest PBL, solved by three half turns.

## Recognition
- Each face shows two opposite colors with no adjacent matches.
- Diagonal arrows point from front-right to back-left on both layers.

## Technique
1. Execute `R2 F2 R2`.
2. Apply AUF as needed.

## Fingertricks
- Use forearm turns for each `R2` and double-thumb pushes for `F2` to avoid overshooting.

## Common Mistakes
- Running the opposite-swap alg and scrambling the cube.

## Practice
- Because it’s so short, focus on accuracy—one lockup ruins the solve.

## Related Cases
- [Ortega-PBL-2](deddal://case/Ortega-PBL-2)

## Pro Tips
- Pre-plan AUF before starting; the alg is over in three moves, so every millisecond counts.
